newsitem.title: ITALY: Scalfaro says Italy will shed light in Somalia.
newsitem.headline: Scalfaro says Italy will shed light in Somalia.

text.p: President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said on Saturday that Italy would seeek to shed light quickly on allegations that Rome's troops had engaged in torture and rape in Somalia.
Scalfaro's office said in a statement that he had met Rino Serri, the foreign ministry undersecretary who is in charge of following Italian affairs in Somalia and is set to visit the African state.

"The head of state asked...Serri to assure the Somali people, and the political and ethnic groups that represent them, that the Italian authorities are determined to shed light quickly on any acts of violence that may have taken place," the statement said.

It added that Italy was ready "to punish any who may have been responsible" for such acts and would "multiply its efforts so that Somalia can be reborn as a united, independent and internationally recognised nation".

The allegations, based on photos and interviews with Italian soldiers who served in Somalia as part of a multinational force from late 1992 to early 1994, have been published over the past weeks in the news magazine Panorama.
The Panorama evidence includes photographs of what appeared to be the sexual assault of a young Somali woman by Italian soldiers using a military flare.
Italy has opened several inquiries into the matter, which has led to the resignations of the commanding officers of Italy's Somali force, generals Bruno Loi and Carmine Fiore.
On Saturday, Italian television reported that General Luigi Cantone, who led some of the troops in Somalia, had been recalled from Albania where he was part of a multinational peacekeeping force.
Television said Cantone's recall was for operational reasons, but cited rumours that the general had been brought back for a probe into his role in Somalia.
The army said on Friday it had suspended Sergeant Antonio Meligeni as a precautionary measure. Meligeni was one of the soliders pictured taking part in an alleged assault.
Also on Friday, army general Nicolo Manca resigned in protest against what he called a "nauseating" campaign against the armed forces over the Somali affair.
Italian army generals have hit back at the allegations, saying many of them were false or exaggerated.
The Panorama allegations have caused deep shock in Italy, a former colonial power in Somalia which has taken pride in the role of its military in peacekeeping efforts abroad.
